claims.statement: The supplied views are product photographs with perspective, not calibrated orthographic drawings.
evidence: reference manifest marks all product views as PERSPECTIVE
claims.modeling_consequence: Use views for ratio and depth constraints, not pixel-traced absolute coordinates.

claims.statement: The dominant body is a shallow circular drum with a deep outer rim, not a tall cylinder or an octagonal planar enclosure.
evidence: front and dimensioned oblique product views
claims.modeling_consequence: Author a sparse 12–16 segment radial shell and reserve radial/longitudinal loops for bezel and rear transitions.

claims.statement: The metallic bezel projects ahead of the white face, while the rear control plate sits behind the shell rim.
evidence: front_left_oblique and rear product views
claims.modeling_consequence: Model the visible front and rear depth hierarchy before any dial graphics or rear-control detail.

claims.statement: The two bells are separate pressed-metal assemblies mounted above the shell.
evidence: front and oblique views show gaps, struts, and distinct material boundaries
claims.modeling_consequence: Keep bells independent and mirrorable; do not pretend they are extrusions of the clock shell.

claims.statement: Each bell is a broad, shallow pressed-metal dome with a rolled lower rim, rather than a horizontal ellipsoid.
evidence: front view highlights and oblique outer contours
claims.modeling_consequence: Use a low-sided authored radial bell profile with a rim loop; reject a scaled sphere if it reads as a capsule.

claims.statement: The carry handle is one continuous thin rod path with a narrow inverted-U profile.
evidence: front view: uninterrupted rod from left mount across top to right mount
claims.modeling_consequence: Use an editable curve or bent cage with only enough controls to match the measured arch.

claims.statement: The two splayed legs create visible triangular gaps between themselves and the lower shell.
evidence: front product view: both lower leg-to-body gaps are visible
claims.modeling_consequence: Validate leg angle, mount point, and foot position as negative-space landmarks before adding collars.

claims.statement: The shell, bells, handle, hammer, and legs are bilaterally arranged about the front vertical centerline.
evidence: front product view
claims.modeling_consequence: Use symmetry only where it preserves the observed manufactured layout; rear controls remain individually placed.

claims.statement: The manufacturer infocard lists 4.56 in length, 2.36 in depth, and 6.49 in height.
evidence: dimensioned product infocard in the reference package
claims.modeling_consequence: Use this as the envelope constraint and preserve uncertainty in all hidden internal dimensions.

claims.statement: Exact bell fasteners, glass retention, and internal rear-shell construction are not visible enough to reconstruct faithfully.
claims.modeling_consequence: Do not invent unseen screws, clips, or internal mechanics; keep interfaces reversible until new evidence exists.

claims.statement: A sparse connected radial shell plus separate bezel, rear plate, and functional assemblies best preserves the visible boundaries and editability.
evidence: shallow-circular-shell
bezel-face-depth
bell-separate-assemblies
leg-splay
claims.modeling_consequence: Do not stack default cylinders for the shell; establish functional loops in one editable radial cage before modifiers.

claims.statement: Flattened UV spheres are rejected for bells because they produce a capsule silhouette and omit the observed pressed-rim transition.
evidence: rejected Stage 01 and Stage 02 solid renders compared with front product view
claims.modeling_consequence: Rebuild bell candidates from a radial profile before any surface-detail pass.

strategies.name: stacked-cylinders-and-scaled-spheres
strategies.rejection_reason: It repeats the rejected generic shell and capsule-bell interpretation instead of preserving the observed continuous shell and pressed-metal bell forms.
